**Tuesday, November 17, 2026 - **

_**Iran:** Iran targets U.S. military facilities in Bahrain for third time.
Qatar announces new talks with Tehran. Iran's Navy says five tankers struck
naval mines near Hormuz. Tehran warns NYT report linking dams to missile sites
could pave way for attacks on civilian infrastructure. CNN goes Judith Miller:
U.S. intelligence warns of suspected Iranian dirty bomb plot, Iran rejects
claim as "fabricated." Only 31% of Americans support U.S. war on Iran. Iran
claims capture of ninth U.S. drone over Qeshm Island; shoots down another._

_**Palestine:** Israeli forces kill two Palestinians in Gaza attacks. Israeli
airstrike hits near UN fuel convoy in Gaza. Israeli settlers kill 72-year-old
Palestinian woman, wound 10 others in Jericho attack. Elsewhere in the
occupied West Bank, Israeli settlers injure eight Palestinians as forces
demolish homes. UK sanctions eight Israeli settlement firms and group blocking
Gaza aid. EU sanctions Gaza outlet over alleged Hamas fundraising._

_**Yemen:** Ansarallah reports nine wounded in Sana'a airstrike. Saudi-backed
forces reinforce defenses around Aden amid Ansarallah advance. Saudi Arabia
replaces Yemen coalition commander following withdrawal from Bab al-Mandab._

_**Lebanon:** Israeli forces continue ceasefire violations across southern
Lebanon. U.S. envoy urges Hezbollah to disarm voluntarily as UN peacekeeping
mandate nears expiration._

_**U.S.:** Hakeem Jeffries moves for recorded leadership vote as Ayanna
Pressley flirts with bid. Permitting reform clears major Senate hurdle.
Forensic scientist argues that evidence strongly points to Epstein homicide.
GOP Rep. DesJarlais concedes his reelection race in Tennessee. Rep. Ro Khanna
suggests $1,700 refund checks for every American to cover costs of Iran War.
White House tells agencies federal employees "must obtain approval" before
agreeing to testify before Congress. Commerce and Justice Departments defend
handling of Megaspeed. Major software outage at Chase Bank._

_**International:** UN report: Drone strikes account for over 80% of civilians
killed in Sudan in first half of 2026. Prominent Bahraini human rights
activist dies at 62. Five European countries announce plan to send rejected
asylum seekers to Rwanda. Nigeria's military says it is receiving U.S.
intelligence and satellite help in strikes on militants. Mongolian president
announces his resignation after accusations of corruption. Costa Rican
journalist shot dead in capital. Russian strikes two Kyiv bridges hours after
Ukraine holds new talks on ending the war._

**This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday**

* * *

# Iran

  * **Iran targets U.S. military facilities in Bahrain for third time:** Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said Tuesday it launched a drone attack targeting a U.S. radar system at Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain, in what it described as a response to repeated violations of Iranian airspace by U.S. military drones. AFP reported explosions in the Bahraini capital, Manama, after the Interior Ministry warned residents of an unspecified danger.

    * U.S. Central Command [denied](https://x.com/CENTCOM/status/2122656792358289747) that the radar system had been hit, saying multiple Iranian drones launched toward Bahrain were intercepted without damaging U.S. equipment or injuring American personnel.

  * **Qatar announces new talks with Tehran:** Qatar said Tuesday that mediation efforts to end the U.S.-Iran conflict were continuing, announcing plans to meet Iranian officials in the coming hours. "Today's meeting with the Iranian side will take place as part of mediation efforts and an exchange of views on the current proposals," Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesperson Majed al-Ansari said during a press briefing in Doha.

    * Warning that "any escalation on the ground poses a challenge to mediation efforts," Al-Ansari urged both sides to exercise restraint and avoid further escalation.

  * **Iran 's Navy says five tankers struck naval mines near Hormuz: **Another tanker [caught fire](https://en.irna.ir/news/86324612/Another-tanker-catches-fire-after-hitting-naval-mine-in-Strait) and sustained severe damage on Tuesday after striking a naval mine east of the Strait of Hormuz, bringing the reported number of tankers damaged in the past 24 hours to five, according to Iran's Navy. The Navy claimed the vessel was traveling through a "prohibited" area with its navigation systems switched off.

    * Separately, Iran's IRGC Navy said a supertanker carrying more than 2 million barrels of crude oil and a liquefied petroleum gas carrier had struck naval mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz. It remains unclear whether the two vessels are included in the Navy's reported total.

  * **Tehran warns NYT report linking dams to missile sites could pave way for attacks on civilian infrastructure:** Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf charged The New York Times of laying the groundwork for further U.S. and Israeli attacks on Iranian civilian infrastructure after the newspaper published an [investigation](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/16/world/middleeast/iran-dams-missile-sites-environmentalists.html) suggesting that some of the country's dams and water transfer projects may have been built partly to support underground missile facilities.

    * The report cited researchers who found that the locations of numerous dams closely overlapped with suspected missile sites targeted in U.S. and Israeli airstrikes this year, although the researchers acknowledged that any connection remains speculative and that many dams serve essential civilian needs.

    * "Prepping the next round on civilian infra," Ghalibaf [wrote](https://x.com/mb_ghalibaf/status/2122556761442058610?a=o3CMBc6bq6L09CduB6g&s=46) on X. "New rule: Any dam, port, or power plant near a U.S. or Israeli base is dual-use. We'll apply your logic consistently and even-handedly."

  * **CNN goes Judith Miller: U.S. intelligence warns of suspected Iranian dirty bomb plot, Iran rejects claim as "fabricated": **U.S. intelligence [suggests](https://edition.cnn.com/2026/11/16/politics/us-intelligence-iran-dirty-bomb) Iran may be developing plans for a possible dirty bomb or chemical weapons attack targeting senior Trump administration officials in Washington, D.C., CNN reported Tuesday. Sources said the intelligence identified specific locations and targets but stressed that there was no evidence Tehran had decided to carry out an attack. The White House said there were "no credible threats to the homeland."

    * Asked about the report, President Donald Trump warned that Iran would "pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before" if it attacked Washington.

    * Iran's UN mission rejected the chemical weapons allegations as "false and fabricated," while Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei accused those who started the war of attempting to manufacture justification for further attacks.

    * Days earlier, Israel Hayom reported that Israel's Mossad had warned the CIA of an alleged Iranian drone plot targeting Trump and senior U.S. officials.

  * **Only 31% of Americans support U.S. war on Iran:** Just 31% of American adults support the U.S. war on Iran, according to a new [Reuters/Ipsos poll](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/trump-approval-holds-near-career-low-32-reutersipsos-poll-finds-2026-11-16/). Trump's approval rating stands at 32%, near the lowest level of his presidency, after falling to a record low of 31% in mid-October.

    * In an interview with Fox News, Vice President JD Vance acknowledged the war's political consequences, citing "the higher gas prices, the higher energy prices," after previously linking the conflict to Republican losses in the midterm elections.

    * "People who want it to become a forever war, they can attack me all they want to because we signed up to not do this," Vance said, accusing some "neoconservatives" of wanting the U.S. to "stay there forever." Vance insisted there was "no daylight" between him and Trump, despite the president recently saying he had told Vance that the U.S. did not need a deal with Iran.

  * **Iran claims capture of ninth U.S. drone over Qeshm Island; shoots down another:** The IRGC [said](https://en.irna.ir/news/86324097/IRGC-seizes-ninth-US-MQM-170-drone-in-electronic-warfare-operation) Tuesday that it had captured another U.S. MQM-170 drone through an electronic warfare operation over southern Qeshm Island, bringing the total number of such drones it claims to have seized to nine. The IRGC said its specialists took control of the aircraft and brought it down intact.

    * Iran's army separately said it shot down a U.S.-made LUCAS attack drone over Hormuz, according to state broadcaster IRIB.

# Palestine

  * **Israeli forces kill two Palestinians in Gaza attacks:** Israeli forces shot and killed a Palestinian man and wounded several others in the Al-Jaafrawi area east of Deir al-Balah in central Gaza on Tuesday, according to WAFA. Separately, a Palestinian succumbed to injuries sustained in an earlier Israeli airstrike in Jabalia, northern Gaza.

  * **Israeli airstrike hits near UN fuel convoy in Gaza:** An Israeli airstrike struck "very close" to a UN-led fuel convoy in Rafah, southern Gaza, on Sunday, [according](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/un-says-israeli-airstrike-hit-very-close-to-un-fuel-convoy-in-gaza/4127036) to the United Nations. UN deputy spokesperson Farhan Haq warned that strikes near humanitarian vehicles, particularly those carrying fuel, expose aid workers to "unacceptable risks," adding that the UN had raised the incident with Israeli authorities. Haq called for increased humanitarian funding and faster entry of essential supplies restricted by Israel.

    * Earlier this month, a senior Palestinian source involved in negotiations [told](https://x.com/dropsitenews/status/2117565707915325674?a=oHcbF_kzkuPMfVLgUIA&s=46) Drop Site that Israel had ordered a complete halt to aid and commercial shipments entering Gaza from Egypt, warning that "fuel and gas come entirely through this route," which handles approximately 50-60 trucks daily.

  * **Israeli settlers kill 72-year-old Palestinian woman, wound 10 others in Jericho attack:** Israeli settlers [shot and killed](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/11/17/%D8%A7%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B4%D9%87%D8%A7%D8%AF-%D9%85%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%B7%D9%86%D8%A9-%D9%88%D8%A5%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%A8%D8%A9-10-%D8%A2%D8%AE%D8%B1%D9%8A%D9%86-%D8%A8%D8%B1%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%B5) a 72-year-old Palestinian woman and wounded 10 other Palestinians during an overnight attack on Ein Al-Duyuk Al-Tahta, west of Jericho in the occupied West Bank, according to WAFA. During the attack, settlers surrounded Palestinian homes while Israeli forces raided the village and closed three entrances to Jericho.

    * Israeli soldiers also severely beat WAFA photojournalist Suleiman Abu Surour while he was covering the attack, leaving him with fractures and bruises. Soldiers detained him for six hours and confiscated his phone before releasing him.

    * Later Tuesday, Israeli forces informed Fheidat's family that they were prohibited from holding a funeral for her in the village.

    * The attack came nearly two weeks after settlers seized eight homes in the village at gunpoint and continued occupying them. **Read Katrine Dige Houm øller's report for Drop Site on the settlers' seizure of homes in Jericho [here](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/jericho-israeli-settlers-palestinians-takeover-soldiers).**

  * **Elsewhere in the occupied West Bank, Israeli settlers injure eight Palestinians as forces demolish homes:**

    * **Bethlehem:** An Israeli settler drove a vehicle into a group of Palestinians gathered near a traffic accident in Tuqu, southeast of Bethlehem, on Monday, injuring eight people, according to WAFA.

    * **Hebron:** Israeli forces [demolished](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/11/17/%D9%85%D8%AD%D8%AF%D8%AB-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%8A%D9%87%D8%AF%D9%85-%D8%AB%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AB%D8%A9-%D9%85%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%B2%D9%84-%D9%88%D8%A8%D8%B1%D9%83%D8%B3%D9%8A-%D8%A3%D8%BA%D9%86%D8%A7%D9%85) three homes sheltering 21 Palestinians along with two livestock sheds and two water wells in the Al-Deirat and Al-Duwarat areas east of Yatta on Tuesday.

    * **Tubas:** Israeli forces [demolished](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/11/17/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD%D8%AA%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84-%D9%8A%D8%B4%D8%B1%D8%B9-%D8%A8%D9%87%D8%AF%D9%85-%D8%A8%D9%8A%D9%88%D8%AA-%D8%A8%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%B3%D8%AA%D9%8A%D9%83%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D9%88%D8%AE%D9%8A%D9%85%D8%A9) greenhouses in Bardala in the northern Jordan Valley. Settlers also destroyed agricultural irrigation networks near Ein Al-Beida.

    * **Occupied** **East Jerusalem:** Settlers [established](https://www.wafa.ps/news/2026/11/17/%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B9%D9%85%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%86-%D9%8A%D9%82%D9%8A%D9%85%D9%88%D9%86-%D8%A8%D8%A4%D8%B1%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%B9%D9%85%D8%A7%D8%B1%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D9%82%D8%B1%D8%A8-%D9%85%D8%AE%D9%85%D8%A7%D8%B3) a new settlement outpost near Palestinian homes in the Al-Hayy area outside Mikhmas, northeast of occupied East Jerusalem.

  * **UK sanctions eight Israeli settlement firms and group blocking Gaza aid:** The UK [announced](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/uk-cracks-down-on-companies-building-settlements-in-the-west-bank-and-groups-blocking-aid-access-into-gaza) new sanctions on Tuesday targeting eight Israeli construction, property development, and architectural firms involved in expanding illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank, alongside Tzav 9, an Israeli group that has organized blockades of humanitarian aid entering Gaza. The sanctions include asset freezes and director disqualifications.

    * "Do not bid, do not build, and do not profit from the destruction of the two-state solution," Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said. The UK said Israel has approved more settlements under its current government than in the previous 20 years.

  * **EU sanctions Gaza outlet over alleged Hamas fundraising:** The European Union announced new sanctions on Monday against Gaza Now, a Gaza-based social media outlet, and its founder, Mustafa Ayash, accusing them of soliciting funds for Hamas and other armed groups, according to the Associated Press. The sanctions include asset freezes for both the outlet and Ayash, who holds refugee status in Austria and will also face a travel ban across the 27-member bloc. Gaza Now has more than 470,000 followers on X and over one million on Telegram, and was previously sanctioned by the United States in 2024.

# Yemen

  * **Ansarallah reports nine wounded in Sana 'a airstrike: **At least nine people were wounded in an airstrike on a shoe factory in the Al-Nahda neighborhood of Sana'a, according to the city's Health Ministry. Ansarallah-affiliated Al-Masirah TV also reported that Saudi airstrikes targeted a demining team in the Kitaf Wa Al-Boqe'e district of Saada governorate.

  * **Saudi-backed forces reinforce defenses around Aden amid Ansarallah advance:** Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces deployed additional troops and military equipment Tuesday around Tur Al-Baha, roughly 85 kilometers (52 miles) from Aden, according to AP. The deployment follows the withdrawal of Saudi-backed forces from positions overlooking the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait, allowing Ansarallah to consolidate control over the area. Ansarallah has repeatedly denied plans to attack Aden.

  * **Saudi Arabia replaces Yemen coalition commander following withdrawal from Bab al-Mandab:** Saudi Arabia [replaced](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/16/saudi-arabia-dismisses-commander-of-coalition-forces-fighting-houthis) the commander of its military coalition fighting Ansarallah on Monday, following the withdrawal of Saudi-backed forces from positions near Bab al-Mandab. King Salman appointed General Fayyad Al-Ruwaili to replace Lieutenant General Fahd Al-Salman, who was reassigned as an adviser to the Saudi defense minister, according to Saudi state media.

    * The leadership change follows weeks of Ansarallah advances along Yemen's Red Sea coast. Saudi-backed forces have struggled to regain territory lost during the offensive, including the key port city of Mocha, while their withdrawal from Bab al-Mandab has allowed Ansarallah to consolidate control near the strait, a critical route for Saudi oil exports amid disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

# Lebanon

  * **Israeli forces continue ceasefire violations across southern Lebanon:**

    * **Bint Jbeil:** Israeli forces [heavily shelled](https://www.nna-leb.gov.lb/ar/news/574666/%D9%82%D8%B5%D9%81-%D9%85%D8%AF%D9%81%D8%B9%D9%8A-%D8%B9%D9%86%D9%8A%D9%81-%D9%8A%D8%B3%D8%AA%D9%87%D8%AF%D9%81-%D9%85%D9%86%D8%B7%D9%82%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D8%B1%D9%8A%D9%91%D8%B4-%D8%A8%D9%8A%D9%86-%D8%A8%D9%84%D8%AF%D8%AA%D9%8A-%D8%AD%D8%A7%D8%B1%D9%8A%D8%B5-%D9%88%D8%AD%D8%AF%D8%A7%D8%AB%D8%A7-2) the Al-Arish area between the towns of Haris and Hadatha on Tuesday, according to Lebanon's National News Agency.

    * **Marjeyoun:** Israeli warplanes [struck](https://www.nna-leb.gov.lb/ar/news/574564/%D8%BA%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%A9-%D9%84%D9%8A%D9%84%D8%A7-%D8%B9%D9%84%D9%89-%D8%AD%D9%88%D9%84%D8%A7-%D9%88%D8%AA%D9%85%D8%B4%D9%8A%D8%B7-%D8%A8%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D8%B3%D9%84%D8%AD%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B1%D8%B4%D8%A7%D8%B4%D8%A9-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AE%D9%8A%D8%A7%D9%85-2) the town of Houla overnight, while Israeli forces opened fire in Khiam.

    * **Nabatieh:** Forces shelled Wadi Al-Salouqi and the hills surrounding the towns of Shaqra and Qabrikha at dawn.

  * **U.S. envoy urges Hezbollah to disarm voluntarily as UN peacekeeping mandate nears expiration:** U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz [called on](https://thearabweekly.com/us-envoy-tells-hezbollah-disarm-voluntarily-restore-state-control) Hezbollah to voluntarily surrender its weapons to the Lebanese army on Monday. "No country can have two armies. I hope and pray Hezbollah will disarm. They should do that voluntarily," Waltz said.

    * He also said he had met Lebanese leaders to discuss alternatives to the UN peacekeeping force in southern Lebanon, whose mandate expires on December 31.

    * In June, Lebanon and Israel signed a framework agreement linking Hezbollah's disarmament to a gradual Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanon and the deployment of the Lebanese army. Implementation has made little progress amid continued Israeli attacks and occupation of Lebanese territory.

# U.S. News

  * **Hakeem Jeffries moves for recorded leadership vote as Ayanna Pressley flirts with bid:** A handful of House Democrats have said recently that they planned to write down the name of Rep. **Ayanna Pressley** (Mass.) in Wednesday's Speaker contest, relying on the tradition of a secret ballot. **Hakeem Jeffries** (N.Y.) subsequently suggested he'll push for a recorded vote, which would make each member's tally public. Jeffries needs 218 votes on the House floor to be elected Speaker. On Monday, Pressley [spoke at a town hall](https://www.instagram.com/reels/Df0qltrvxP7/) in Boston about the race in the most open terms she had yet, but did not announce an official challenge: "I'm very humbled to even be in conversation when I think about the history of this seat that I occupy--**Tip O 'Neill **served in this seat, the Speaker of the House; **John F. Kennedy** served in this seat--this is a historic seat and we have had a historic electoral outcome. We are on the precipice of a historic vote for Speaker and we need to have a historic impact on Congress because that is the decisive mandate by the people, that we move with boldness, not timidity. Scared power isn't power at all. When you have the power you have to use it. Now I am making no declarations or announcements here. What I will say is that I do not need to be the Speaker of the House to speak for the people."

  * **Permitting reform clears major Senate hurdle:** The Senate moved to end debate on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) by a 70-27 margin Monday evening, setting it up for final passage. Twenty-one [Democrats joined Republicans](https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_votes/vote1192/vote_119_2_00264.htm) in backing the bill that has the support of both the clean energy and the fossil fuel industries. Its cornerstone provision aims to massively expand transmission capacity, the lack of which is a fundamental obstacle to the buildout of clean energy, but which can also be used to transmit dirty energy. Some environmental advocates whose approach leans more heavily on litigating against energy projects--clean and dirty alike--argued Congress should wait until Democrats control both chambers and can write a better bill. Massachusetts Sen. **Ed Markey** , the lead Senate sponsor of the Green New Deal resolution, delivered a [lengthy address](https://www.youtube.com/live/4xRXAeYGTjQ) Monday against the bill. The bill's backers counter that the approach ignores the reality that the legislation needs the signature of President Trump and, unless the filibuster is removed, at least some support from Republican senators. Passing BAAJA during the lame duck, meanwhile, would not bar the next Congress from working on improving it.

  * **Forensic scientist argues that evidence strongly points to Epstein homicide:** Forensic scientist **Michael Freeman** has begun [presenting](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/16/us/jeffrey-epstein-autopsy-michael-freeman.html) the findings in his year-long inquiry into **Jefferey Epstein 's** death, saying Epstein's injuries are most plausibly explained by homicidal strangulation. Freeman, who studies bias and error in death investigation, based his analysis on the autopsy file, given to him by Epstein's brother **Mark Epstein**. He claims the photos show fingernail marks above the ligature, evidence of neck abrasion and a deep shoulder hemorrhage, all of which point to struggle. His findings have been rejected by scientific journals so far, and some forensic pathologists agree the mark was atypical but say the images could still fit suicide. The New York City medical examiner's office says "it stands by its determination" of suicide.

  * **GOP Rep. DesJarlais concedes his reelection race in Tennessee:** Tennessee**** GOP Rep. **Scott DesJarlais** [conceded](https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/6196424-victoria-broderick-scott-desjarlais-tennessee-4th/) to Democrat **Victoria Broderick** on Monday in an unexpectedly close race to represent Tennessee's 4th District. Decision Desk HQ has not projected a winner, with Broderick leading 48.87% to 48.73% (a lead of just over 200 votes). She won despite being heavily outspent in a district Trump carried by 24 points in 2024. DesJarlais has served eight terms in Congress.

  * **Rep. Ro Khanna suggests $1,700 refund checks for every American to cover costs of Iran War:** Rep. **Ro Khanna**(D-Calif.)****[proposed](https://thehill.com/the-120/6223191-khanna-proposes-iran-war-refunds/) $1,700 refund checks for every American to reimburse Americans for the economic costs of the Iran War, arguing the checks would compensate for higher gas, food, and electricity prices from war-related oil transport disruptions. He urged the House and Senate to pass the proposal in the first week of January ("let's put it on Trump's desk"). Moody's **Mark Zandi** estimates the war has cost households an average of $2,000.

  * **White House tells agencies federal employees "must obtain approval" before agreeing to testify before Congress:** In a Monday memo to agency general counsels, Politico reported, White House counsel **Will Scharf** [said](https://www.politico.com/live-updates/2026/11/16/congress/white-house-not-playing-ball-01168250) agency personnel "must obtain approval" from the White House Offices of Legislative Affairs and Counsel before appearing at congressional committees. The directive comes a week after Scharf warned incoming House Oversight Chair **Robert Garcia** that Democratic investigations "may cross the line into blatant criminality," as Democrats prepare to scrutinize Trump, his family, and business interests next year.

  * **Commerce and Justice Departments defend handling of Megaspeed:** The Commerce and Justice Departments issued a rare joint statement defending their handling of Megaspeed, the Singapore chip buyer at the center of Nvidia's alleged spy scandal, after Treasury Secretary **Scott Bessent** accused Commerce of failing to stop Nvidia's sales to the firm. Citing "inaccurate information circulating in public reporting," the statement said Commerce opened a probe in 2024 and that DOJ now leads a criminal case. They did not explain why Megaspeed was never blacklisted. President Trump said Monday that Commerce Secretary **Howard Lutnick** "might have delayed" doing so to avoid "a blow-up with China." Trump also cast doubt on the spy allegations against Megaspeed CEO **Alice Huang** , whose affair with Nvidia CEO **Jensen Huang** forced his resignation last week: "I don't know that she's a spy. Nobody's proven that," while adding that he "wouldn't mind" Huang returning. The turmoil sent Nvidia down 4.1% Monday and dragged the tech-heavy Nasdaq down 2.5% ahead of the company's quarterly earnings after the bell Tuesday.

  * **Major software outage at Chase Bank:** A software bug at JPMorgan Chase [disrupted](https://www.usnews.com/news/business/articles/2026-11-16/customers-at-some-of-the-nations-largest-banks-are-reporting-difficulty-accessing-accounts-online) online banking and Zelle transfers for thousands of customers at several major U.S. banks on Monday. A Chase spokesman said Monday the issue was "a software bug in an on-premise hardware system--it is not cyber-related," with other banks affected "only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us." Zelle's owner, Early Warning Services, said its network was fully operational. The disruption followed a Thursday Microsoft outage, Friday's FAA ground stop, and a United Airlines system outage Monday that delayed departures.

# Other International News

  * **UN report: Drone strikes account for over 80% of civilians killed in Sudan in first half of 2026:** Drone strikes have come to be a "defining feature" of the war in Sudan, accounting for more than 80% of the civilians killed in the first six months of 2026, according to a new [report](https://www.ohchr.org/en/documents/country-reports/human-rights-situation-sudan-1-january-30-june-2026) by the UN Human Rights Office. The report documents the targeting of civilians and civilian infrastructure, indiscriminate attacks, and the continued use of sexual violence as a weapon of war. At least 2,230 civilians were killed in Sudan between January until the end of October, with the actual civilian casualty figures likely to be higher, the report found. Civilians in the Kordofan region were the most heavily impacted, accounting for more than two-thirds of documented civilian casualties, followed by the Darfur region, where most of the remaining casualties occurred. "The findings in our report provide more evidence, if any were needed, of the ceaselessly unbearable civilian suffering of the war in Sudan and the warring parties' continued and brazen disregard for the laws of war," UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk said.

  * **Prominent Bahraini human rights activist dies at 62:** Nabeel Rajab, a prominent Bahraini human rights activist who helped lead the country's 2011 pro-democracy protests and spent years in prison for advocating political freedoms and freedom of expression, died Tuesday at the age of 62. His wife and daughter found him unresponsive at their home in Istanbul, Turkey. Rajab, a co-founder and former president of the Bahrain Center for Human Rights, was repeatedly arrested following the Saudi-backed crackdown on Bahrain's 2011 uprising. He was sentenced to five years in prison over social media posts criticizing the Saudi-led war in Yemen, before being released to home detention in June 2020. Rajab left Bahrain earlier this year amid a renewed crackdown on protests following the outbreak of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, [telling](https://apnews.com/article/bahrain-nabeel-rajab-arab-spring-rights-b037ae40a69a0f78a4e4eed36bb6e58f) the Associated Press that he feared arrest following Bahraini authorities torture of an imprisoned activist. In one [post](https://x.com/nabeelrajab/status/2096867866330956285?a=UHygzNxNEh8JaPcEsb8&s=46), he shared footage of the destruction in Gaza, writing, "How will the people of this land, which has been reduced to rubble, and their future generations ever forgive our silence, whether we are governments or ordinary people?"

Rwanda's interior minister, Vincent Biruta, said arrivals could return home, integrate in Rwanda, or move to another country where they can legally reside, claiming that the mechanism would employ an "independent monitoring mechanism" and cooperate fully with UNHCR. Germany's interior minister said it differs from the scrapped 2022 UK deal, which the UK Supreme Court ruled unlawful because Rwanda was not a safe third country, because only those whose claims are rejected would be sent.
